prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create one high-fidelity desktop web application screen for CommandGrid, a hackathon infrastructure recovery simulator. Render edge to edge, landscape 16:10, crisp readable interface text, no browser frame, no device, no desk. This is a static design exploration with fictional sample data, not a landing page or poster.
Direction A — spatial atlas. The operator's job is to spot a degraded facility, select an incident, and execute a recovery action. Lead with a beautifully crafted spatial topology map of a fictional river valley and three facilities: North Haven Relay, Cedar Support Center, Juniper Power Station. Low-relief terrain and refined engineering diagram annotations make infrastructure relationships tangible; restrained amber status markers indicate a power incident. Keep the map legible and functional.
The frame contains CommandGrid as simple text, navigation Dashboard / Mission Builder / Objectives / Mission Control / Reports, with Mission Control active. Mission title “Communications Recovery”. Status “Running”; elapsed “03:42 / 10:00”; Pause control. A compact metric band: Communications 82%, Equipment 75%, Power 64%, Resources 58%. Incident detail “Power failure” at Juniper Power Station, recovery action “Activate backup power”, cost “8 resources”. A discreet lower activity and telemetry region.
Art direction: mineral blue-gray and glacier white with deep petrol ink, amber reserved for warnings. Technical humanist sans typography, lucid generous whitespace. One dominant spatial composition, precise understated chrome, a quieter right incident inspector. Inspired by ambitious Awwwards spatial storytelling and Impeccable's hierarchy discipline. No neon glow, glass cards, decorative sci-fi HUDs, purple gradients, oversized marketing slogans, invented logos or testimonials. Include a small “Sample scenario” label. Make the complete working UI feel designed, not generic.
approval: User explicitly requested implementation matching A across all screens, using real data.
